cards.explanation: The answer is that they stand firm in it. Paul says the gospel is what he preached to them, what they received, and what they "stand firm" in (1 Corinthians 15:1). That's a church planted like a tree. I think Paul is smiling a little as he writes it.

The answer is that they hold firmly to the word he preached. Paul says, "By this gospel you are saved, if you hold firmly to the word I preached to you." (1 Corinthians 15:2) So that little "if" points right back to the word he preached. Hold on to it, friends, like a baker holds a hot tray with two good mitts.

The answer is False. Paul says that without holding firmly to the word he preached, "…you have believed in vain." (1 Corinthians 15:2) So believing doesn't still count for something in that case. It's like pulling a tray out of a cold oven. You did all the stirring, and nothing came of it.

The word is received. Paul says, "For what I received I passed on to you as of first importance…" (1 Corinthians 15:3) He's a delivery guy here, not the inventor. He got it, and he handed it on. I know that feeling, because somebody handed me a whole new life once.

The answer is on the third day. Paul says Christ "…was raised on the third day according to the Scriptures…" (1 Corinthians 15:4) The list goes death, burial, raised, and the burial isn't the final word. The third day is where the story turns.

The answer is True. The phrase shows up twice in a row. Christ died for our sins "…according to the Scriptures…" and He was raised on the third day "…according to the Scriptures…" (1 Corinthians 15:3-4) Same phrase for the death and for the raising. Count them, friends, there are two.

The answer is the Twelve. Paul says Christ "…appeared to Cephas and then to the Twelve." (1 Corinthians 15:5) Cephas is the name Jesus gave Simon, which is translated Peter (John 1:42). The Twelve are the disciples Jesus called to Him (Matthew 10:1). So the Twelve are next on Paul's list.

The answer is more than five hundred. Paul says Christ "…appeared to more than five hundred brothers at once…" (1 Corinthians 15:6) Five hundred! That's a bigger crowd than any bakery line I've ever seen. And they all saw Him at the same time.

The answer is False. Paul says the more than five hundred are "…most of whom are still living, though some have fallen asleep." (1 Corinthians 15:6) So most are still alive when he writes. Only some have fallen asleep.
The answer is True. Paul says, "And last of all He appeared to me also…" (1 Corinthians 15:8) He puts himself at the very end of the list. The man holding the pen is the last name on it.

The answer is that he persecuted the church of God. Paul says he's unworthy "…because I persecuted the church of God." (1 Corinthians 15:9) He doesn't hide it or dress it up. He says it plain, and I respect that.

The answer is the grace of God. Paul says, "But by the grace of God I am what I am…" (1 Corinthians 15:10) He gives God the credit. The least of the apostles didn't climb up there, he was given a hand.

The answer is True. Paul says, "…I worked harder than all of them…" (1 Corinthians 15:10) Then he quickly adds, "…yet not I, but the grace of God that was with me." So he names his hard work and hands the credit right back to God's grace.

The word is preach. Paul says, "Whether, then, it was I or they, this is what we preach, and this is what you believed." (1 Corinthians 15:11) Paul and the other apostles all preach the same message. And the Corinthians believed it, which is good news for them.
